paper_title: Knowing You Don't Know Learning When to Continue Search in Multi-round   RAG through Self-Practicing
caption: Ablation study on different Critic model choices. Both follow the SIM-RAG setting with GPT-4 as the Reasoner, but the blue bar uses learned Flan-T5-783M as a Critic, while the red bar uses GPT-4 as the Critic (a.k.a., self-critique).
model_annotation: The chart illustrates an ablation comparison of two Critic model choices in a SIM-RAG setting across multiple QA datasets/metrics, with paired bars showing performance for “Flan-T5-783M” as the Critic versus “GPT-4” as the Critic (self-critique). The horizontal axis contains six categorical conditions in left-to-right order: “TriviaQA (EM),” “HotPotQA (EM),” “2Wiki (EM),” “TriviaQA (F1),” “HotPotQA (F1),” and “2Wiki (F1),” with no additional axis label shown; the vertical axis is a numeric score scale (unlabeled) shown on a linear scale spanning roughly 25 to 85, with major tick labels at 25, 45, 65, and 85 (regular 20-point intervals). Each category has a grouped pair of vertical bars: the blue bar (legend: Flan-T5-783M) and the red bar (legend: GPT-4), with values printed on the bars. For TriviaQA (EM), the blue bar is 77.3 and the red bar is 77.1; for HotPotQA (EM), blue is 37.0 and red is 31.9; for 2Wiki (EM), blue is 44.5 and red is 32.5; for TriviaQA (F1), blue is 82.8 and red is 83.8; for HotPotQA (F1), blue is 49.7 and red is 43.3; and for 2Wiki (F1), blue is 53.3 and red is 38.1. The grouped bars are arranged side-by-side within each category (blue on the left, red on the right), the categories are not sorted by value, and the only visual emphasis is the use of distinct colors and the numeric annotations on each bar.
